summary: Bala Sahai Shastri was an Indologist. He held positions at Panjab University, where he was attested as Assistant in 1932 and as in-charge of the Sanskrit Section in 1947.

Baladora Indrajothi specializes in Indology and Buddhist studies. Educated at the Oriental Studies Society and University of Kelaniya, he held teaching posts at Vidyalankara Pirivena (2008–2015), University of Kelaniya (2016–2019), and Bhiksu University of Sri Lanka (2019–2021).

Balaganapathi Devarakonda works in philosophy and Indology. He studied at the University of Delhi (M.A., 1993–1995) and the University of Hyderabad (PhD, 1997–2004), later becoming a Professor at the University of Delhi in 2015.

Baliram Shukla works in the fields of philosophy and Indology. He has held positions at Savitribai Phule Pune University, serving as Head of the Department of Philosophy (attested 2001) and as Professor (attested 2026).
Balram Shukla is an Indologist and linguist. He was educated at the University of Delhi, where he became a Professor in 2004.

Balthasar Bickel is a scholar in linguistics and Tibetology who studied at the University of Zurich (~1985–1997). He held a post at the University of Leipzig (~2002–2011) and served on the editorial board at Zurich (~2011).

Bangwei Wang is an Indologist, Sinologist, and Buddhist studies scholar who completed his doctoral dissertation at Peking University in 1987. He served there as Professor, Professor of Indian and Buddhist Studies, and eventually Boya Retired Professor (attested 2000–2026).

Banikanta Kakati was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Cotton University, Presidency University, and the University of Calcutta. He was a professor at Cotton University (1918–1947) and later a Dean and department head at Gauhati University (1948).

Bapu Deva Sastri was an Indologist who studied at Sehore Sanskrit School under Lancelot Wilkinson, Dhundiraja Misra, and Sevarama. He served as a teacher at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University from 1842 to 1889.

Barbara A. Holdrege is a scholar of religious studies and Indology. She has held posts at the University of California, Santa Barbara, as Associate Professor of the Comparative History of Religions (attested 2000) and Professor (attested 2026).

Barbara Ambros is a Japanology, religious studies, and Buddhist studies scholar educated at Columbia and Harvard. She held teaching appointments at several institutions, including Columbia and International Christian University, before becoming Professor at UNC Chapel Hill in 2015.

Barbara Catharina Jacoba Timmer was a scholar in Indology and philosophy. She completed her education at Leiden University (~1916–1922) and the University of Amsterdam (Ph.D., ~1922–1930), studying under Marcel Cohen, Barend Faddegon, and Jean Philippe Vogel.

Barbara Diane Miller was a scholar in Tibetology who completed her B.A. at the University of Michigan (1948) and her Ph.D. at the University of Washington (~1948–1958). She held teaching posts at Beloit College and the University of Wisconsin-Madison.

Barbara E. Ward was a Sinologist educated at Cambridge and London. She held academic posts at the University of London, Cambridge, and CUHK, and served as head of the International Institute for Environment and Development in 1973.

Barbara Gerke is a religious studies and Tibetology scholar who earned her D.Phil. at Oxford under Charles Ramble and Geoffrey Samuel. She held research posts at Berlin and Oxford, followed by a faculty position at the University of Vienna.

Barbara Harriss-White is an Indology scholar who attended Newstead Wood School. She worked at the University of East Anglia (~1979–1990) and later served at Queen Elizabeth House, Wolfson College, and the University of Oxford as Emeritus Professor of Development Studies.

Barbara Mittler is a Sinologist and historian who studied at Pearson College London, the Mandarin Training Center, the University of Oxford, and Heidelberg University. She held a post at Heidelberg University in 1993.

Barbara Nimri Aziz is a scholar in Tibetology and religious studies. She earned her B.A. from Queen's University at Kingston and her Ph.D. from SOAS under Christoph von Fürer-Haimendorf, later holding a post at the University of Oran in 2007.

Barbara Stoler Miller was an Indologist educated at Barnard, Columbia, and Penn under W. Norman Brown, Stella Kramrisch, and Royal W. Weiler. She spent her career at Barnard College and Columbia University, and served as AAS president in 1990.

Barbora Sojková is an Indology and religious studies scholar educated at Charles University, UCL, and Oxford, where she earned her DPhil. In 2025, she held postdoctoral researcher posts at the University of Oxford and the University of Zurich.
